absent: Transition rules and owners that move the global system state between boot, running and terminal power phases.
Complete parameter list and return contract of the link restriction callback beyond its visible destination ring argument.
Configuration conditions selecting among the alternate dyntick, idle, I/O wait and key helper variants.
Behavior, errors and side effects of request tag, reject-and-link, architecture cpustat and virtual time helpers owned elsewhere.
Quota accounting, expiry and revocation timing, watcher delivery and associative array layout for keyrings.
Sleep semantics and allowed calling contexts for the underlying sleep check behind the conditional helper.
Binary layout guarantees such as sizes, alignment and padding for the described structures beyond field order.

findings.text: Provides a conditional sleep-point helper that evaluates its argument once and only invokes the underlying sleep check when the argument is true; a false argument performs no action.

Defines the global boot and power lifecycle with distinct phases for early booting, scheduler availability, init memory release, steady running, and terminal halting, power off, restart and suspend. The ordering progresses from booting toward running and then toward one of the terminal power states.
Declares a build marker indicating that dynamic ftrace causes a rebuild; its presence alone signals the condition without carrying a value.

Establishes a family of file-read purposes covering firmware and both plain and compressed kernel modules, kexec image alongside kexec initramfs, plus security policy, certificate, an unknown fallback and a maximum sentinel. Two generator helpers derive enumeration constants with a common prefix and matching string spellings from a single list, keeping numeric codes and names aligned.
Offers a small translator from identifier to human readable label that returns the matching table entry for valid codes and falls back to the unknown label when the code is outside the table.

Defines per-CPU time accounting buckets including idle and I/O wait, user and nice levels, system time, hard and soft interrupt time, steal time, guest execution with a guest nice variant, an optional force-idle bucket under core scheduling, and a final count sentinel that sizes the storage array.

Holds per-CPU accounting centered on an array named cpustat indexed by usage bucket. When tickless idle support is enabled it additionally carries a flag named idle_dyntick for dyntick state plus a flag named idle_elapse for elapsed indication, a sequence guard named idle_sleeptime_seq, a timestamp named idle_entrytime and a two element steal record named idle_stealtime.
Aggregates interrupt accounting with a total counter named irqs_sum for hard interrupts and a table named softirqs with one entry per soft interrupt type.
Exposes helpers to reach per-CPU statistics for the current processor and for an explicitly numbered processor, separately for interrupt totals and for CPU time breakdowns.

Specifies that incrementing affects only the calling processor soft interrupt slot, that single-slot reads select a processor and interrupt number, and that per-processor summation iterates over every soft interrupt type to produce a total.

States that interrupt snapshotting is a no-operation in this configuration and that querying deltas since a snapshot always yields zero, while fetching a processor hard interrupt total returns its stored aggregate.
Defines one configuration where dyntick start and stop plus interrupt enter and exit hooks do nothing and where the idle dyntick query constantly reports inactive.
Describes a variant where idle and I/O wait queries for a given processor forward to architecture supplied routines rather than reading the generic array.

Describes alternate variants where idle and I/O wait queries read the corresponding array slots for the requested processor, where one dyntick query reflects the current processor stored flag and another constantly reports inactive.

Requires that generic field reads divert idle and I/O wait requests to their dedicated accessors while serving all other buckets directly from the array, that bulk fetch copies the whole per-CPU record then refreshes those two special buckets, and that public wrappers simply forward to these defaults.
Specifies that tick accounting for a task flushes virtual time only when the processor is not in dyntick idle; dyntick idle ticks skip the flush.

Carries proposed key material with a pointer for the original description and a separate pointer for the proposed description, a payload union, a raw data pointer with its length, a quota length distinct from raw length, and an expiry timestamp. The layout is marked for randomization.
Defines a callback type for in-kernel key request handling that receives an authority key plus opaque auxiliary data and reports success or failure as an integer.
Groups search inputs with a comparison hook defaulting to exact description match, a raw data pointer, a scratch slot for preparsed state, and a lookup mode selector.
Provides two lookup selectors where direct description lookup is 0x0000 and iterative search is 0x0001.

Organizes each key type around a name string, a default data length for quota estimation, and a flags word, plus hooks to vet descriptions, to preparse and release proposed payloads, and to instantiate or update keys with quota reservation. Update callers must hold the key against concurrent reads.

Extends each type with optional match preparsing and cleanup, revocation under write lock and destruction, description and read access under read lock with full-size reporting and null-buffer size probing, a synchronous request handler, a restriction lookup returning null for permissive known names or an invalid error for unknown names, asymmetric query and operation entry points, and internal linkage plus a lock class. The whole record is marked for layout randomization.
Assigns KEY_TYPE_NET_DOMAIN to 0x00000001 for a network namespace domain and KEY_TYPE_INSTANT_REAP to 0x00000002 for immediate reaping after expiry.
Specifies that negating a key and linking it into a keyring is equivalent to rejecting with a key-not-found error using the same timeout and ring linkage.
Fixes serial numbers as signed thirty-two bit values and permission masks as unsigned thirty-two bit values.

Reserves the high permission byte for possessor rights where KEY_POS_VIEW is 0x01000000 and KEY_POS_READ is 0x02000000, while KEY_POS_WRITE uses 0x04000000 and KEY_POS_SEARCH uses 0x08000000, plus KEY_POS_LINK at 0x10000000 and KEY_POS_SETATTR at 0x20000000, with KEY_POS_ALL at 0x3f000000 covering all six.

Places user rights in the third byte where KEY_USR_VIEW is 0x00010000 and KEY_USR_READ is 0x00020000, while KEY_USR_WRITE uses 0x00040000 and KEY_USR_SEARCH uses 0x00080000, plus KEY_USR_LINK at 0x00100000 and KEY_USR_SETATTR at 0x00200000, with KEY_USR_ALL at 0x003f0000.

Places group rights in the second byte where KEY_GRP_VIEW is 0x00000100 and KEY_GRP_READ is 0x00000200, while KEY_GRP_WRITE uses 0x00000400 and KEY_GRP_SEARCH uses 0x00000800, plus KEY_GRP_LINK at 0x00001000 and KEY_GRP_SETATTR at 0x00002000, with KEY_GRP_ALL at 0x00003f00.

Places third-party rights in the low byte where KEY_OTH_VIEW is 0x00000001 and KEY_OTH_READ is 0x00000002, while KEY_OTH_WRITE uses 0x00000004 and KEY_OTH_SEARCH uses 0x00000008, plus KEY_OTH_LINK at 0x00000010 and KEY_OTH_SETATTR at 0x00000020, with KEY_OTH_ALL at 0x0000003f. An undefined mask KEY_PERM_UNDEF is all bits set at 0xffffffff.

Enumerates needed permissions including view, read and write, search and link, attribute change and unlink, with an unspecified starter value and special overrides for administrator, possession of an authorization token, and deferred checking. Lookup control defines KEY_LOOKUP_CREATE as 0x01 and KEY_LOOKUP_PARTIAL as 0x02, with KEY_LOOKUP_ALL combining both.
Tracks domain tag lifetime with an RCU callback head, a reference count and a boolean marking removal of the subject.

Holds a hash in field hash plus a word sharing member x that overlays a short prefix in field desc with its size in field desc_len, where the two small fields swap order by endianness, followed by a type pointer in field type, a domain pointer in field domain_tag and a full string pointer in field description.
Provides a payload view that can be read as an RCU protected pointer or as four generic data slots sharing the same storage.
Encodes a key reference with possession in the low address bit, where construction ORs the flag, extraction masks it away to recover the pointer, and testing isolates the bit.
Declares a link restriction callback whose visible first argument is the destination ring, and a restriction record pairing that checker with an authorizing key and an allowed key type.
Restricts explicit state codes to uninstantiated and positively instantiated, leaving rejection errors to be carried as negative state values.

Starts each key with a reference count and serial number, a union that serves either as graveyard linkage or as a serial tree node, an optional watcher list under notification support, a read-write semaphore separating changes, an owner pointer and opaque security data.

Continues with a union holding either expiry or revocation time, a last-use timestamp for reclamation, user and group identifiers, a permission mask, short quota and data lengths where data length may differ from the RCU visible payload which must self-describe size, a short state carrying positive codes or negative rejection errors, and an optional debugging magic.

Defines status bit positions where KEY_FLAG_DEAD is 0 and KEY_FLAG_REVOKED is 1, while KEY_FLAG_IN_QUOTA is 2 and KEY_FLAG_USER_CONSTRUCT is 3, plus KEY_FLAG_ROOT_CAN_CLEAR at 4 and KEY_FLAG_INVALIDATED at 5, with KEY_FLAG_BUILTIN at 6 and KEY_FLAG_ROOT_CAN_INVAL at 7, and KEY_FLAG_KEEP at 8 with KEY_FLAG_UID_KEYRING at 9 and KEY_FLAG_USER_ALIVE at 10. Debugging magic KEY_DEBUG_MAGIC is 0x18273645.

Aliases the type and description lookup key in two views sharing storage: a structured index with hash and description metadata, and an expanded view exposing hash, description length, type pointer, domain tag and description pointer. Any change here must stay aligned with the standalone index structure.

Overlays key data with keyring linkage so the same area can hold a generic payload union or, for rings, a name link plus an associative array of members, followed by an optional link restriction pointer that defaults to open when absent and is set only through designated allocators.

Controls allocation with KEY_ALLOC_IN_QUOTA at 0x0000 for strict quota, KEY_ALLOC_QUOTA_OVERRUN at 0x0001 to allow overrun, KEY_ALLOC_NOT_IN_QUOTA at 0x0002 to bypass quota, plus KEY_ALLOC_BUILT_IN at 0x0004, KEY_ALLOC_BYPASS_RESTRICTION at 0x0008, KEY_ALLOC_UID_KEYRING at 0x0010 and KEY_ALLOC_SET_KEEP at 0x0020.

Requires active reference handling to increment the usage count and return the same pointer, to tolerate null by returning null, and to release a reference by unwrapping the possession bit before dropping the count.

Warns that one configuration replaces core key operations with inert shims where validation always succeeds, serial and possession queries return zero, pointer and lookup helpers return null, reference acquisition returns null, and put, revoke, invalidate, reference put, credential change, init, namespace release and domain removal do nothing.

Provides request entry points where the basic form forwards to a tag aware helper with no domain, while network forms derive the domain from the supplied namespace, with an RCU variant that omits callout information.

Specifies that serial extraction tolerates null by yielding zero, that state reads use acquire ordering against concurrent instantiation, and that positivity means equality with the positive code while negativity means any value below zero.

Restricts payload access so RCU readers use an RCU dereference, locked readers use a protected dereference asserting the semaphore is held, and writers publish through an RCU assignment. Type callbacks document read locking for reads, write locking for revocation, and exclusion against reads for updates.
Reserves distinct preprocessor guards for the read-file, statistics, key type, key and keyboard headers to ensure single inclusion.
